answer: I'd like to talk about someone who made a big difference to me when I first moved to Dhaka. A time I received invaluable help was when I was moving to the capital to start university and felt completely overwhelmed by everything. I had never lived away from home before, and the size and noise of the city frightened me a little. I remember my mother packing enough food for a week, as if Dhaka had no restaurants. A senior student from my hometown, who was already in his third year, went out of his way to help me settle in. My father had got his number from a family friend, and he met me at the bus station on my very first day. He helped me find accommodation, showed me around, and introduced me to people, which was incredibly [[generous]] of him. He even taught me which buses to take and where to find cheap but decent food near campus. Without his support, those first few weeks would have been far more [[daunting]] and lonely. What struck me was that he expected absolutely nothing in return; his kindness was completely [[selfless]]. I remember feeling deeply [[indebted]] to him, especially since we had barely known each other before. His help made an enormous difference to how quickly I adjusted. Honestly, the experience reminded me how much a small act of kindness can mean to someone in a vulnerable situation. It also inspired me to be equally [[supportive]] when I later saw first-year students struggling to settle in. I still remember his generosity fondly.

followUps.q: Are you still in contact with him?
followUps.answer: Yes, we still message each other now and then. He works in Dhaka now, and whenever I visit my elder sister there, I try to meet him for a cup of tea.

followUps.q: Do you think people help each other more in small towns or big cities?
followUps.answer: In small towns, I think. People know each other, so helping feels natural. In big cities, people are kind too, but they are often too rushed to notice when someone is struggling.

note: Persona fix: he lives and works near home, so 'moving to a new city for work' became moving to Dhaka for university, helped by a senior student from Sirajganj; plain 'grateful' replaced by 'indebted', added 'selfless'.
